config.title: Auth Context

intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple authentication context in Angular to manage user login state across your app. You'll learn how to use Angular's dependency injection and services to create a centralized, reusable authentication system. The main technologies involved are Angular services, RxJS BehaviorSubject for state management, and TypeScript interfaces. By the end, you'll have a functional auth service that components can use to check login status and user data.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is essential in any application requiring user authentication and authorization. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce platforms like Amazon where user login status determines shopping cart access and personalized recommendations. In banking apps like Chase, auth context controls which accounts and transaction histories are visible to authenticated users. Social media platforms like Facebook use it to manage feed personalization and privacy settings based on logged-in users. As a developer, you'll implement auth context to secure dashboard access, protect API endpoints, and personalize user experiences across entire applications.

objectives: Implement an authentication service to manage user login state
Configure dependency injection to provide the auth service throughout the application
Construct an authentication context component to share auth state
Bind authentication state to UI components for conditional rendering
Initialize protected routes that require authentication
Integrate authentication state with Angular's change detection
Manipulate auth state through login and logout actions

steps.title: Create BehaviorSubject for auth state
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthService class, declare a private property named 'authState$' of type 'BehaviorSubject<AuthState>' and initialize it with the initialAuthState object.
steps.hint: Use the RxJS BehaviorSubject class to create a reactive stream that holds the current authentication state. Remember to import BehaviorSubject from 'rxjs'.

steps.title: Create auth state observable
steps.instruction: In your AuthService, create a public observable property named 'authState$' that exposes the BehaviorSubject's value as an observable stream for components to subscribe to.
steps.hint: You can create an observable from a BehaviorSubject by accessing its 'asObservable()' method. This property should be public so components can access it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have a public 'authState$' observable property that components can subscribe to for receiving auth state updates.
successCriteria: AuthService has a public 'authState$' observable property created from the BehaviorSubject using 'asObservable()'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Implement login method
steps.instruction: Add a login method to your AuthService that updates the authState$ BehaviorSubject with authenticated state (user logged in).
steps.hint: The method should call next() on the BehaviorSubject with the new state object containing isAuthenticated: true and a username.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your AuthService will have a login method that updates the auth state observable to reflect an authenticated user.
successCriteria: The AuthService contains a login method that calls next() on the BehaviorSubject with an object having isAuthenticated: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a login method, but make sure it updates the BehaviorSubject with the correct authenticated state object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login method is missing or doesn't properly update the auth state. Check that it calls next() on the BehaviorSubject with { isAuthenticated: true, username: ... }.

steps.hint: The logout method should call next on the authStateSubject with the initialAuthState object.

steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component named AuthContext that will serve as the provider for AuthService to its child components.
steps.hint: Use the Angular CLI command 'ng generate component AuthContext' or manually create the component files with the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new AuthContext component is created with proper Angular component structure.
successCriteria: AuthContext component is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-auth-context', and basic template containing <ng-content>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with proper selector and template.

steps.title: Add AuthService to AuthContext providers
steps.instruction: In the AuthContext component's @Component decorator, add AuthService to the providers array to make it available through dependency injection.
steps.hint: Look for the @Component decorator in the AuthContext component and add providers: [AuthService] to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will be available for injection within the AuthContext component and its child components.
successCriteria: AuthService is listed in the providers array of the AuthContext component's @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
